entry.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
entry.summary:
Quantum resistance in Bitcoin addresses is a subject of growing importance, particularly in anticipation of the potential impact of cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC). The discussion emphasizes that while certain address types, such as P2WPKH, become vulnerable once their public keys and signatures are exposed, there exist alternative address formats that maintain quantum resistance even after this information has been revealed. This distinction is crucial for long-term security planning within the Bitcoin network.
Highlighting the urgency, it is noted that preparations for quantum resistance must be made prior to the actual emergence of CRQC. Delaying these measures could result in significant loss; for example, millions of bitcoins could be at risk if adequate protections are not implemented before quantum computing threats materialize. Therefore, proactive adoption of quantum-resistant technologies and practices is essential to safeguarding assets against future vulnerabilities.
The exchange underscores the value of ongoing research and clear communication within the development community. By identifying which address types offer continued protection post-public key and signature exposure, developers and users can make informed decisions to enhance the security and resilience of the Bitcoin ecosystem.
